title: Add Momentum Mode to Capture Trending Regime Profits Being Left on Table
analysis: On 2026-05-22, the bot attempted 5 consecutive AAPL BUY entries with signals 'RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25 (trending)' — all correctly rejected by duplicate-position logic, but all carrying a 2.0 R:R and HIGH/MEDIUM confidence. rationale: The strategy is systematically blind to an entire market regime. When ADX>30 fires, the bot goes dark rather than pivoting to trend-following entries. The signal detection logic already identifies these setups (AAPL, AMD, QQQ momentum scores of 4-5), the R:R is confirmed viable (2.0:1), and the macro regime is aligned. insight.expected_effect: Converts near-zero-trade days (May 25: 13+ consecutive skips despite 4 HIGH-confidence signals) into active trading days. Based on QQQ entry on May 22 (submitted, 2.0 R:R, score=5), momentum trades in this regime carry equivalent or superior R:R to mean reversion setups.
insight.risks: Momentum entries in late-stage trends risk buying the top. Late-cycle momentum trades (RSI>80) carry higher reversal risk. Must enforce strict ADX minimum, recency of breakout, and reduced position sizing (1% risk vs 1.5%) for momentum mode to avoid overexposure at trend exhaustion.

title: Signal Contamination: Bot Is Generating Momentum Signals Inside Mean Reversion Scorer
analysis: On 2026-05-22, five AAPL entries fired signals 'RSI>65 (strong momentum), AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25 (trending)' with signal_score=4. These are anti-signals for mean reversion — RSI>65 is overbought, not oversold. Yet the scoring engine assigned score=4, meeting the 2+ threshold required for entry. The SIGNAL SCORING section in CLAUDE.md only defines RSI<35 (+2), RSI<45 (+1), BelowBB (+1), BelowMA20>1% (+1), ADX<25 (+1) — all mean reversion signals. There is no defined rule for how RSI>65 or AboveMA20 generates a score of 4. This means the bot is operating a shadow scoring system for momentum signals that is not documented in CLAUDE.md, has no defined minimum threshold specific to momentum, and is routing those scores through the mean reversion entry gate. The only reason these didn't execute was the duplicate-position block on AAPL — not because the risk rules correctly filtered them. The QQQ momentum trade on 2026-05-22 DID execute (score=5, SUBMITTED) under these undocumented rules.
rationale: Undocumented scoring pathways are a systemic risk. The QQQ trade on May 22 executed under momentum signals using the mean reversion R:R gate and position sizing. If that trade had been a loss, it would have been attributable to a strategy the system was never designed to run. CLAUDE.md must explicitly define the momentum signal scoring rubric, its entry conditions, and its separation from mean reversion sizing rules — or momentum scoring must be disabled until the momentum mode is formally sanctioned (see suggestion 1).

insight.why_now: The QQQ SUBMITTED trade on 2026-05-22 is direct evidence that momentum trades are already executing live under undocumented rules. This is not a future risk — it is a current operational gap. With 4 open positions already held and account at ~$99k, an undocumented execution pathway is a capital protection failure.
insight.purpose: Enforce auditability and intentionality. Every executed trade must be traceable to an explicit rule in CLAUDE.md. Undocumented scoring means the weekly review cannot correctly attribute wins/losses to strategy logic.
insight.expected_effect: Closes the gap between what CLAUDE.md says the bot does and what it actually does. Prevents accidental momentum execution under mean reversion position sizing during unfavorable conditions (e.g., late-trend entries with RSI>80).
insight.risks: Disabling momentum scoring entirely while the regime is trending (ADX>30) would return the bot to the zero-trade condition seen on May 25. The correct path is to document and gate momentum scoring formally, not eliminate it.

title: BTC/USDT Is Generating Null Signal Data — Remove or Fix Crypto Data Pipeline

rationale: A data pipeline returning '?' for all indicators is a silent failure mode. The bot is not erroring out — it is silently evaluating broken data and producing structured skip entries that look normal in the log. The frozen account value ($99,062.18 for 33+ hours across a trading day) and static open_positions=4 with zero P&L delta is a strong indicator of a state management bug, potentially triggered by the crypto data failure. BTC/USDT mean reversion suitability is also questionable: crypto exhibits higher volatility regimes, lower mean reversion reliability, and the current Binance/CCXT integration appears unreliable. insight.purpose: Restore data integrity and eliminate false-negative skip cycles caused by broken indicator feeds. Prevent state freeze from propagating into the next trading session.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminating broken BTC/USDT cycles restores the bot's ability to correctly identify and act on the best available equity candidate during each cycle. Resolving the position state freeze ensures P&L tracking and open_positions limits are accurate.

title: Add Momentum/Trend-Following Sleeve to Capture Dominant Regime
analysis: Across all 50 journal entries, the system generated ZERO executed trades despite detecting high-confidence momentum signals repeatedly. On 2026-05-25 and 2026-05-26, the best candidates logged were AAPL (RSI=80.46–81.45, ADX=38.14–42.34, momentum score=4) and AMD (RSI=73.15–77.93, ADX=56.71–57.97, momentum score=5) — both flagged as TRENDING and correctly rejected by the mean reversion filter. The account sat at ~$99,062–$100,108 for the entire observation window with open_positions locked at 4–5 (existing holds), generating no new alpha. The macro context confirms this is not a mean reversion environment: SPY is 2.35% above its 20-day MA (750.59 vs 733.36), Technology sector is up +6.87% over 5 days, and VIX is 17.01 — elevated enough to suppress deep oversold dislocations but not high enough to warrant sitting out entirely. The system correctly identifies trending instruments but has no strategy module to act on them, leaving a structural alpha gap every session.
rationale: A pure mean reversion system is regime-dependent by design. In a trending regime (ADX>30 on leading names, SPY above MA20, Tech +6.87% in 5 days), mean reversion signals will be structurally absent for the dominant instruments. Adding a momentum sleeve — activated only when ADX>30 and RSI>65 on a 20-day high breakout — allows the system to harvest returns from the regime it is actually in, rather than waiting for a regime it is not in. This is not strategy dilution; it is regime-adaptive capital deployment. The two modules are complementary: mean reversion fires in ranging markets, momentum fires in trending markets, and the ADX threshold (already in Rule 6) gates which module is active.

insight.why_now: On 2026-05-25 and 2026-05-26 alone, AMD scored momentum=5 with ADX=56–57 and AAPL scored momentum=4 with ADX=42 across 15+ consecutive cycles. These are textbook trend-following setups the system saw, logged with HIGH confidence, and was structurally forbidden from trading. The opportunity cost is not theoretical — it is documented in the journal.
insight.purpose: Unlock a second strategy module that activates in the trending regime the current watchlist is already exhibiting, converting detected-but-skipped HIGH-confidence signals into executable trades.
insight.expected_effect: In trending regimes (ADX>30, SPY>MA20, sector momentum positive), the momentum sleeve should generate 2–5 new trade entries per week on the existing watchlist. At the observed R:R of 2.0:1 (as seen in the AMD BUY on 2026-05-26 at entry 495.78, stop 470.52, target 546.30) and 1.5% risk per trade, each executed trade targets ~$2,250 gain on a ~$100K account. Even a 45% win rate at 2:1 R:R produces positive expectancy (EV = 0.45×2 − 0.55×1 = +0.35R per trade).
insight.risks: Momentum strategies are vulnerable to sharp reversals; a late-cycle entry on AAPL at RSI=81 carries mean-reversion risk from the opposing module's own signals. Requires strict position independence — a momentum long on AMD must not coexist with a mean reversion long on AMD. Also risks regime misclassification during transitions (ADX crossing 30 threshold).

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER & REGIME ROUTING: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. Instead, route to MOMENTUM MODULE: entry permitted if (a) RSI > 65, (b) price above MA20 by >1%, (c) 20-day high breakout confirmed on above-average volume, (d) ADX > 30, and (e) R:R ≥ 1.5:1 with stop at 0.75x ATR below entry. Momentum entries use identical position sizing (1.5% risk) and are subject to all hard rules. A symbol may not simultaneously hold a mean reversion position and a momentum position.

title: Remove BTC/USDT From Active Scanning Until Data Feed Is Operational

ADX=? regime=?' indicating a completely non-functional data feed. During this same window, the account_value remained completely flat at $99,062.18 across all 29 BTC/USDT-dominated entries, confirming zero productive activity.
rationale: A candidate with RSI=?, ADX=?, regime=? should score 0 and should never surface as 'best candidate.' Its repeated appearance as best candidate indicates the equity scanner is either exhausted (all positions full or no signals) or the candidate ranking logic does not penalise missing data. Keeping a broken instrument in the active universe wastes compute cycles, pollutes the journal with non-informative entries, and creates false impression of market scanning activity. Either fix the Binance/CCXT feed or gate BTC/USDT behind a data-quality check that requires all required fields to be non-null before the symbol enters candidate ranking.

insight.purpose: Eliminate null-data candidates from surfacing in best-candidate logs, reduce journal noise, and ensure the system's scan output reflects only evaluable instruments.

title: Implement Opportunity Cost Logging to Quantify Regime Mismatch in Real-Time
analysis: The system correctly skipped all trending signals per its rules, but there is no mechanism to quantify what those skips cost in forgone P&L. AMD was detected at entry 495.78 with R:R=2.0 on 2026-05-26; by the same session the account was up only $1,029 (1.03% day gain) from existing positions. Meanwhile AMD's momentum score of 5 with ADX=56.88 represents a near-ideal trend entry. AAPL with RSI=81.39 and ADX=42.34 was similarly skipped 8+ times on 2026-05-26. The system has no way to flag to its operators: 'This regime has been TRENDING for N consecutive sessions; mean reversion signal frequency has dropped X%; estimated forgone momentum P&L is $Y.' Without this signal, the operator cannot make an informed decision about when to activate an alternative module or expand the universe to include range-bound instruments better suited to current conditions.
rationale: Regime mismatch is the single largest structural risk to a single-strategy system. The journal data shows the system has been in a near-zero new-entry state for at least 5 consecutive trading days (May 22–26) while holding the same 4–5 positions. This is a regime lock-out, not disciplined patience. A real-time regime health metric — tracking the ratio of TRENDING skips to total evaluations, consecutive days without a new mean reversion entry, and the cumulative momentum signal score of skipped candidates — would allow the operator to make evidence-based decisions about strategy routing rather than discovering the regime mismatch only in weekly review.

insight.why_now: 50 entries, 0 new executed trades, 4–5 positions unchanged throughout. The system has been regime-locked for the entire observable window. This is only visible in retrospect by counting journal entries; it is not surfaced as an operational alert.
insight.purpose: Surface regime mismatch as a real-time operational signal so that strategy routing decisions (activating momentum module, expanding watchlist to range-bound ETFs, or reducing scan frequency) can be made proactively.
insight.expected_effect: Faster operator response to regime transitions, reduced opportunity cost from prolonged single-regime lock-out, and a documented basis for strategy configuration changes that is grounded in observed signal data rather than intuition.
insight.risks: Overly sensitive regime alerts could prompt premature strategy switching. The metric should require a minimum threshold (e.g., 3 consecutive trading days with <1 mean reversion entry AND >50% of best-candidate slots occupied by TRENDING skips) before triggering an alert, to avoid noise during normal slow-signal periods.

title: Add Momentum/Trend Layer: Bot Detects Signals It Cannot Act On
analysis: Across 50 journal entries spanning May 25-27, the bot executed ZERO new trades. The dominant rejection pattern is not a signal quality problem — it is a structural mismatch: the bot repeatedly identifies high-scoring momentum setups (AAPL RSI=81.97, ADX=43.89; AMD RSI=77.93, ADX=56.88; IWM with AboveMA20+ADX>25) scoring 4-5 points, then discards them entirely because it has no mechanism to act on them. On May 26 alone, 10+ consecutive cycles flagged AAPL or AMD as best candidate in MOMENTUM mode with scores of 4-5, and every single one was logged as SKIP. The macro environment confirms this is not a fringe condition: SPY is 2.06% above its 20-day MA (750.46 vs 735.29), Technology sector is up +4.12% in 5 days, and key watchlist names show ADX readings of 43-57 — deep into trending territory that has persisted for the entire observation window. The system is architecturally blind to the dominant regime. The USO skip on May 27 (score=4, signals: RSI<45, BelowLowerBB, BelowMA20>1%, ADX<25) was the only genuine mean reversion candidate in the entire 50-entry dataset — and it was blocked by the max positions rule (5/5 open). The bot is fully allocated in a market where its held positions are presumably drifting while its scanner finds nothing tradeable under current rules.
rationale: A pure mean reversion system in a trending regime is not just suboptimal — it is structurally idle. The scanner is already computing momentum scores (Mom=4, Mom=5) and regime classification (regime=TRENDING) internally. The infrastructure to detect these setups exists; the bot simply has no code path to act on them. Adding a momentum strategy module — even a conservative one limited to high-ADX, high-RSI breakout continuation entries with ATR-based stops — would convert currently-wasted scan cycles into executable opportunities. This is not parameter tuning; it is filling a structural gap that the journal data proves exists across multiple consecutive trading days.

insight.why_now: The journal shows 3 consecutive trading days (May 25-27) where the bot's own scanner identified AAPL and AMD as 4-5 point momentum candidates on every single cycle, yet the system had zero mechanism to act. This is not a one-off regime anomaly — ADX readings of 42-57 on core watchlist names represent an entrenched trending environment. The Technology sector +4.12% 5-day performance and SPY above MA20 confirm the macro context is actively hostile to mean reversion opportunity generation.
insight.purpose: Create a secondary execution path for momentum/breakout setups when ADX > 30 and the mean reversion pipeline is dry. This transforms the bot from a single-strategy system that goes dormant in trending regimes into a regime-adaptive system that maintains throughput regardless of market character.
insight.expected_effect: Directly addresses the core problem visible in this journal: near-zero trade execution rate. Even 1-2 momentum trades per day during trending regimes, at the existing 1.5% risk / 1.5:1 R:R minimum, would meaningfully improve capital utilization. Historically, momentum strategies in strong trending environments (ADX>40, RSI>70 continuation) carry win rates of 45-55% with R-multiples of 1.8-2.5 when entries use pullback confirmation rather than pure breakout chasing.
insight.risks: Momentum strategies underperform sharply during whipsaws and regime transitions. Adding momentum capability without a hard regime gate risks the bot entering trend trades just as the trend exhausts. Must be gated by: (1) ADX > 30 confirmed on D1 timeframe, (2) entry on intraday pullback to EMA20 rather than at new highs, (3) separate daily loss limit tracking per strategy module, (4) momentum trades must NOT share position slots with open mean reversion trades at max capacity.

When ADX > 30 AND the mean reversion pipeline produces no qualifying entries AND open_positions < MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS, the bot MAY evaluate momentum continuation setups under the MOMENTUM execution path: entry requires (a) ADX > 30, (b) RSI > 60 but < 80, (c) price pulling back to EMA20 on intraday chart (not chasing new highs), (d) R:R ≥ 1.5:1 using ATR-based stop below EMA20, (e) signal_score ≥ 3 from momentum scoring group. The watchlist is dominated by names that (a) are actively trending away from mean reversion suitability or (b) are broken/returning no data. If the watchlist is populated with trending momentum names, the mean reversion scanner will find nothing — by design, because the trend filter correctly rejects them. Adding 4-6 instruments with documented mean reversion properties (broad ETFs, sector ETFs in non-trending regimes, liquid defensive names) directly increases the probability of finding qualifying mean reversion setups per scan cycle. Separately, the BTC/USDT data issue must be resolved or the symbol removed — it is appearing as best candidate in 18/50 cycles while returning zero actionable data, which means the scanner is frequently terminating on a dead-end candidate.

insight.why_now: The journal proves the current watchlist cannot generate mean reversion signals in the prevailing environment. 50 cycles, 0 executed mean reversion trades. The one qualifying mean reversion setup (USO, May 27) was blocked by position limits, not by signal quality. The watchlist needs instruments that are ranging or mildly declining — sectors with negative 5-day performance (Energy -4.7%, Financials -0.46%) are natural hunting grounds for mean reversion in the current macro context.
insight.purpose: Increase the density of qualifying mean reversion opportunities per scan cycle by replacing or supplementing trending momentum names with instruments that have structural range-bound tendencies and are currently in or near oversold conditions. Fix or remove the BTC/USDT data feed issue to stop it from polluting scanner output.

ETFs like XLE (Energy, -4.7% 5d), XLF (Financials, -0.46% 5d), GLD, or TLT are diversified instruments with natural mean reversion properties and are currently in the correct regime for the strategy. This addresses idle capital without requiring any strategy logic changes.

Adding too many instruments also increases correlation risk if multiple sector ETFs are held simultaneously during a broad market drawdown. Watchlist additions should be screened for: (1) historical ADX < 25 frequency > 50% over trailing 6 months, (2) correlation < 0.7 with existing open positions.

title: Max Positions Cap Creating Opportunity Cost: 5/5 Blocked the Only MR Signal in 50 Entries
analysis: On May 27 at 14:35, USO fired a legitimate mean reversion signal (RSI<45, BelowLowerBB, BelowMA20>1%, ADX<25 — score=4, all 4 signals valid, including 3 classical oversold signals). This was the single qualifying mean reversion setup across the entire 50-entry observation window. It was skipped not due to signal quality or R:R failure, but because open_positions was at 5/5 (the hard cap). The 5 open positions being held at that moment are exclusively from prior entries — none of which appear in this journal window as new entries, meaning the portfolio may be holding positions opened before the observation period that have since become deadweight. The daily P&L on May 27 was consistently negative (-$47 to -$209 range throughout the day), suggesting the held positions were moving against the account rather than contributing. The hard cap of 5 positions, when fully occupied by underperforming holds, creates a structural blockade that prevents the strategy from acting on new opportunities — which in this case meant missing the only qualifying signal in 3 trading days.
rationale: The 3-day time stop exists precisely to prevent stale positions from occupying slots indefinitely. However, the current framework does not differentiate between a position in its first 24 hours (high relevance, should be protected) and a position approaching its time stop (declining relevance, should potentially be exited earlier if a higher-quality signal is blocked). A tiered position management rule — where positions in day 3 can be exited early to free capacity for new qualifying signals — would prevent the scenario observed here. Additionally, the correlation-adjusted risk framework should be applied: if 3+ of the 5 open positions are equity longs in a rising market, they are effectively a single correlated position, and the nominal '5 max' cap understates actual concentration risk.

insight.why_now: The May 27 USO skip is the clearest evidence in the dataset that the position cap is acting as an opportunity cost mechanism rather than purely a risk control. The bot was at 5/5 all day on May 27, the account was down ~$80-$209 intraday, and the one valid mean reversion signal was blocked. This is the exact scenario where the time stop should be proactively applied to free capacity.
insight.purpose: Ensure the position cap functions as a risk control (preventing overexposure) without also functioning as an opportunity cost trap (blocking new high-quality signals when existing positions are stale or underperforming). Introduce a capacity management rule that proactively evaluates whether aging positions should be exited to accommodate new qualifying signals.
insight.expected_effect: In the observed scenario, this rule would have triggered early exit of the oldest open position (approaching day 3) to free a slot for the USO mean reversion trade — the only qualifying signal in 50 cycles. More broadly, this rule improves capital rotation efficiency during periods where positions age out without hitting take profit, which is common in low-volatility ranging environments (VIX 16.29).
insight.risks: Exiting positions early to chase new setups introduces a form of opportunity cost in the other direction — the exited position might have hit its target the following day. The rule must be bounded: early exit for capacity should only trigger when (a) the candidate new signal scores 4+ points with at least 2 classical oversold signals, (b) the position being considered for early exit has been open 2.5+ days (past 83% of the 3-day time stop), and (c) the position being exited is currently within 0.25x ATR of breakeven or better (do not exit losers early to chase new trades).

The regime filter (Rule 6: ADX>30 = no new MR entries) is working correctly, but it has no companion rule to evaluate whether EXISTING MR positions should be defensively exited when the regime shifts to trending. A mean reversion position in a trending instrument is a position that may never reach its take-profit target at MA20 — the MA20 itself is moving away. insight.purpose: Add a regime-change exit rule: when the portfolio-level regime shifts from ranging to trending (ADX crosses above 30 on SPY as market proxy), existing MR positions should be evaluated for early exit — specifically those that are at breakeven or in profit. This frees slots for momentum entries and removes capital from a hostile regime.
insight.expected_effect: Faster capital rotation out of stale MR positions into regime-appropriate setups. Reduces the 'frozen portfolio' condition visible across all 50 journal entries where 5 slots are occupied but zero action is taken.
insight.risks: Exiting MR positions early on a regime shift could prematurely close winners if the regime shift is brief (ADX spikes then reverts). A confirmation filter (ADX>30 sustained for 2+ consecutive days on SPY before triggering regime-exit review) would reduce false triggers.

title: Cycle frequency pattern: 8-10 minute re-evaluation loops during losing days suggest latent overactivity pressure
analysis: On 2026-05-27, four cycles fired between 17:21 and 19:44 (83 minutes, ~20-minute cadence) with day_pl deteriorating from -72.50 to -251.65 — all skips, but the system kept cycling. On 2026-05-28, the system ran 17 cycles between 11:24 and 19:43 (8+ hours), with cycles as tight as 6-8 minutes apart (e.g., 12:33→12:40→12:48, then 13:36→13:50→14:14→14:24→14:29). On 2026-05-29, during a losing period (day_pl deteriorating from -89 to -437 between 10:37 and 13:36), cycles ran every 10-20 minutes across 9 consecutive skips. While the system correctly SKIPped all of these, the high-frequency cycling pattern during drawdown periods creates a structural pressure scenario: if thresholds were ever slightly loosened (or a borderline signal fires), the system would be primed to act on a suboptimal setup. The 2026-05-29 USO BUY at 12:26 (execution_status=CANCELLED, during a -173 drawdown period) shows the system did attempt an entry during the intraday drawdown, suggesting the cycle pressure is real. The MSFT BUY at 10:37 on 2026-05-29 also fired with momentum signals (RSI>65, AboveUpperBB, AboveMA20) — signals that are antithetical to mean reversion — and was only stopped by execution cancellation, not by rule rejection.
rationale: The MSFT entry on 2026-05-29 with signals ['RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveUpperBB', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)'] and signal_score=5 is the most concerning data point: this is a pure momentum profile being attempted by a mean reversion system. The execution_status=CANCELLED saved the trade, but the fact that it reached BUY action with zero mean reversion signals suggests the signal composition rule (Rule 10) may not be preventing all overbought entries. If day_pl was -89 at the time, the system may have been under implicit pressure to find a trade. Adding a minimum inter-cycle delay during negative day_pl periods (e.g., minimum 30 minutes between evaluation cycles when day_pl < -100) would structurally prevent the rapid-fire re-evaluation pattern without degrading signal quality.

insight.why_now: The MSFT BUY on 2026-05-29 is the clearest evidence: a mean reversion system generated a BUY signal with ['RSI>65', 'AboveUpperBB', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25'] — every single signal is the opposite of mean reversion. This happened at the start of a day that went on to lose -437 by 13:36. The combination of early loss + rapid cycling + wrong-direction signal is the behavioral fingerprint of pressure-driven overactivity.
insight.purpose: Install a structural cooldown that prevents the system from cycling into suboptimal entries during drawdown periods. This is not about reducing opportunity — in a trending regime with ADX>30, there are no valid mean reversion entries anyway. The cooldown simply formalizes what the SKIP logic already does, while removing the latent pressure of rapid re-evaluation.
insight.expected_effect: Elimination of the MSFT-class error where momentum signals leak through into BUY actions during mean reversion mode. Reduction in the number of CANCELLED executions (which represent near-misses on bad trades). No expected reduction in valid trade capture since the trending regime produces zero valid mean reversion entries regardless of cycle frequency.
insight.risks: A hard cooldown timer could theoretically cause the system to miss a genuine mean reversion setup that emerges quickly after a false signal. Set the cooldown to activate only when (a) day_pl < -150 AND (b) ADX > 25, since these are the conditions under which the pressure pattern manifests. In ranging markets with day_pl near zero, normal cycle frequency is appropriate.

proposed_rule: DRAWDOWN COOLDOWN (new rule 13): When day_pl < -150 AND ADX > 25 (trending regime, no valid mean reversion entries expected), enforce a minimum 30-minute gap between evaluation cycles. Log each suppressed cycle as 'COOLDOWN_SKIP: drawdown cooldown active (day_pl=X, ADX=Y, next eval after HH:MM)'. This prevents pressure-driven re-evaluation loops during periods where the regime structurally precludes valid entries. Additionally, Rule 10 (SIGNAL COMPOSITION) must explicitly reject any entry where ALL fired signals are from the overbought/momentum group {RSI>65, AboveUpperBB, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25} — this was not caught on the MSFT BUY at 2026-05-29T10:37 and must be hardened.

title: Cycle frequency is 10-30 min intraday — scan rate exceeds signal persistence, creating noise
analysis: On 2026-06-12, NVDA was scanned 10 times between 12:12 and 14:22 with RSI values of 44.19, 44.19, 44.09, 44.11, 44.46, 43.98, 43.73 — a range of less than 0.73 RSI points across 130 minutes. META was scanned 6 times on the same day with RSI ranging 32.31–34.56 across 5.5 hours. These are not independent signals — they are the same signal re-evaluated every 15-30 minutes with negligible change. On 2026-06-15, AMD was scanned as MOMENTUM mode 6 times between 13:49 and 15:36 with RSI oscillating 65.06–65.28 and ADX static at 33.02 throughout. The system is running at a cadence that generates no new information between cycles. This creates an illusion of activity (50 journal entries over ~2 trading days) while producing zero trades. More subtly, if the system ever does execute, the same setup could theoretically trigger duplicate entries within a single session if the position-check logic has any latency — the USO BUY on 2026-06-15 at 12:54 was followed by an AMD attempt at 13:29 just 35 minutes later with open_positions already showing 1, suggesting the executor is cycling fast enough to attempt new entries before prior ones fully settle.
rationale: Intraday mean reversion on daily Bollinger Bands and 20-day MA targets does not benefit from sub-30-minute re-evaluation. The signal inputs (RSI, BB, MA20, ADX) are computed on daily or hourly bars — their values are nearly identical across consecutive 15-minute scans. Reducing scan frequency to once per 90 minutes during market hours (or implementing a minimum-change threshold before re-evaluating a symbol) would reduce noise, prevent near-duplicate journal entries, and free computational cycles. It would also make the journal more analytically useful — currently, identical SKIP entries for the same symbol 10 minutes apart provide no diagnostic value.

insight.why_now: The 50-entry journal covers roughly 2 trading days with near-zero trades. The entries are not 50 independent decision points — they are 10-15 unique market states re-sampled 3-5 times each. This pattern will make weekly review analysis misleading (win rate, signal frequency stats will be distorted by duplicate near-identical entries) and suggests the scan loop is running faster than intended.
insight.purpose: Improve signal independence, reduce journal noise, and prevent the weekly review metrics from being polluted by near-duplicate entries. A minimum inter-scan interval also reduces the risk of accidental duplicate order submission in fast-cycling conditions.
insight.expected_effect: Journal entries drop from ~25/day to ~8-10/day while capturing the same decision points. Weekly review statistics become meaningful. No impact on trade quality since signal values are not changing meaningfully between scans. Potential side benefit: if scan cycles consume API quota (Alpaca, Binance), reducing frequency extends the available quota for genuine signal changes.
insight.risks: A longer scan interval could miss a rapid intraday mean reversion setup that develops and resolves within 30 minutes. However, given the strategy targets the 20-day MA as take profit, the relevant holding period is 1-3 days — missing the first 30 minutes of a setup entry is immaterial to the trade's outcome. The only genuine risk is missing a fast-moving stop-loss trigger, but that is handled by the hard stop order placed at execution, not by the scan loop.

proposed_rule: 12. SCAN FREQUENCY: The minimum interval between full watchlist scans is 90 minutes during equity market hours (09:30–14:55 EST). A symbol that was evaluated and SKIPPED due to insufficient score change (all indicator values within 2% of prior scan) must not be re-evaluated until the next scan cycle. Exception: if a position is open and price has moved more than 0.5x ATR since last check, a targeted re-evaluation of that symbol is permitted at any time for stop/exit management. Crypto scans follow exchange hours but observe the same 90-minute minimum between full scans. Rapid re-scanning of the same symbol within a single session without meaningful indicator change MUST be logged as SCAN_SKIP (not a trading SKIP) to preserve journal integrity.

title: Cycle-frequency spike on loss days indicates potential system-level overpolling, not revenge trading
analysis: On 2026-06-16 (daily P&L ranging from -$649 to -$519 throughout the session), the system generated 18 journal entries in a single day — compared to 6 entries on 2026-06-12 (flat P&L day) and roughly 17 entries on 2026-06-15 (positive P&L day peaking at +$130). title: Strategy identity violation: QQQ entered on trending/momentum signals

This suggests the signal scoring logic does not adequately distinguish between 'score ≥ 2' and 'score ≥ 2 with at least 1 oversold signal', allowing the Rule 10 check to be bypassed or miscounted.

insight.why_now: The QQQ position entered on 2026-06-17 is still reflected in open_positions=7 throughout all of 2026-06-18 (50 entries later), meaning this single rule violation is actively suppressing performance across a multi-day window. insight.purpose: Prevent momentum/trending signal combinations from masquerading as mean reversion entries by enforcing Rule 10 as a hard gate in the signal composition check, with explicit logging when the gate fires.

title: Frozen Account Value on June 19 Signals Executor or Data Feed Failure Requiring Circuit Breaker
analysis: Across all 20 journal entries on June 19 (10:40 EST through 17:57 EST), the account_value is exactly $98,628.69 with day_pl_at_decision=0.00 for every single cycle. This is statistically impossible during live or realistic paper trading — account value should fluctuate as the 7 open positions mark to market throughout the day. The precision (to the cent, identical across 7+ hours) confirms this is not rounding — the account value feed is frozen or returning a cached value. The system is running 20 decision cycles against stale data, logging HIGH confidence SKIPs, and consuming compute while effectively blind. Separately, the June 17 entries show day_pl oscillating normally (-$1,172 to -$877), confirming the freeze began on June 19. The executor or Alpaca account feed appears to have stopped updating, yet the bot continued cycling without detecting or escalating the anomaly.
rationale: A trading system that cannot detect its own data feed failure is operationally unsafe. The current rules have no staleness detection on account_value or position mark-to-market. Adding a data integrity check — specifically a variance check on consecutive account_value readings — would have caught this on cycle 2 of June 19 and halted further cycles until the feed was confirmed live. This is a risk management gap independent of strategy quality.

insight.why_now: The June 19 data shows 20 consecutive cycles of identical account value across 7 hours. This is happening now and the system has no mechanism to self-detect it. Every cycle run against frozen data is a wasted cycle that could also mask a real trading problem (e.g., a position that hit its stop but wasn't reflected in the frozen feed).
insight.purpose: Add an account data staleness circuit breaker that halts new decision cycles if account_value has not changed across N consecutive cycles during market hours. Forces human review before resuming.
insight.expected_effect: Prevents the system from operating in a degraded data state, which could lead to incorrect position sizing (based on stale account value), missed stop-loss events not reflected in the feed, or false confidence in position count accuracy.
insight.risks: On genuine low-volatility days, account value may change very slowly but the feed is still live. The check should require zero change (to the cent) across at least 3 consecutive cycles during market hours before triggering, not merely small changes. After-hours cycles naturally show flat account values and should be excluded from this check.

insight.purpose: Protect capital during corrective market phases by reducing per-trade risk exposure on mean reversion longs when the macro backdrop is unfavorable, while still allowing the strategy to participate in valid technical setups.

In winning scenarios, profits are proportionally reduced but the strategy remains profitable. The primary benefit is drawdown reduction during prolonged corrections, not return enhancement.

title: Cycle storm pattern: 10–15 min re-evaluation loops on stale data producing zero signal drift
analysis: On June 19, the system ran 17 evaluation cycles between 10:40 and 19:35 EST — all skipping on the same MSFT data (RSI=33.33, ADX=18.46, unchanged across all cycles). This is not a trading behavior problem — it is a system architecture problem manifesting as a behavioral anti-pattern: the bot is simulating 'activity' (high cycle frequency, journal entries logged) while producing zero informational value. The frozen account_value on June 19 also masks whether positions actually exist — if open_positions=7 but account_value is static, the position data feeding the cap check may itself be stale, which could mean slots are being held by ghost positions.
rationale: A cycle that cannot change its decision because (a) the position cap is hit and (b) market data has not materially changed since the last cycle is pure overhead. Beyond efficiency, the frozen account_value pattern on June 19 is a data integrity flag: if the account snapshot is not refreshing between cycles, the position cap check (open_positions=7) may be reading from a cached state rather than live broker data. This would explain why MSFT signals score 4–5 internally but the agent reports signal_score=0 in the output — the scoring pipeline may be running on live data while the execution gate checks stale cached positions. At 0.75% risk per trade with a 1.5:1 R:R, a 50% win rate still produces positive expectancy. Protects the account from the scenario where MSFT/NVDA/TSLA oversold positions are entered at full size and the market continues lower through the time stop.
insight.risks: If the correction reverses sharply (short-squeeze or macro catalyst), reduced position sizing means less profit capture on the initial move up. This is an acceptable tradeoff for capital preservation in the current environment.

title: Confidence field mismatch: HIGH confidence on zero-signal SKIP cycles indicates metadata corruption
analysis: Between 2026-07-01T16:05 and 2026-07-01T17:57, the journal records 10 consecutive SKIP entries for BTC/USDT (mode=NONE, score=0, RSI=?, ADX=?, regime=?) — all with confidence='HIGH'. This is a direct contradiction: HIGH confidence is being logged on cycles where no signals fired, no symbol was selected (symbol='NONE'), and market data was unavailable (RSI=?, ADX=?). Separately, the 2026-07-01T14:57 entry logs confidence='HIGH' with signal_score=0, open_positions=5, day_pl=-$28 — again, HIGH confidence on an empty evaluation. The day_pl at the start of this HIGH-confidence SKIP cluster was -$286 (16:05), declining from the afternoon peak of ~+$297. The pattern suggests the confidence field is being populated by a fallback default ('HIGH') rather than computed signal quality during crypto-hours evaluations when Binance data is unavailable.
rationale: Corrupted confidence metadata undermines the integrity of the weekly review process. The WEEKLY REVIEW PROMPT instructs the agent to identify signal combinations that performed best — if HIGH confidence is assigned to null-data cycles, any confidence-stratified performance analysis will be skewed. More critically, if a future execution layer uses confidence as an input to position sizing or entry decisions, HIGH confidence on zero-data cycles is a live risk. The BTC/USDT mode=NONE pattern across 10+ cycles also indicates the crypto sleeve is generating evaluation overhead with no productive output — the scoring engine is running but producing only noise.

insight.why_now: The 10 consecutive HIGH-confidence/zero-signal BTC entries on 2026-07-01 afternoon (16:05-17:57) represent the largest single cluster of metadata-corrupt entries in the visible journal window. This follows a period where day_pl turned negative (-$286 at 16:05) and the equity market closed, leaving only crypto evaluation cycles active. The pattern will recur every trading day during after-hours if not corrected.
insight.purpose: Ensure confidence field integrity so that performance analytics, weekly reviews, and any future confidence-weighted position sizing are based on signal quality rather than fallback defaults. Secondarily, prevent the BTC/USDT scoring engine from running evaluation cycles when market data is unavailable (RSI=?, ADX=?).
insight.expected_effect: Clean confidence metadata immediately improves weekly review signal — the system will correctly identify that BTC/USDT is currently generating zero tradeable signals and allow a strategic decision about whether to keep it in the universe. No direct P&L impact, but prevents downstream sizing errors if confidence is ever used as a position size multiplier.
insight.risks: The root cause may be in the executor/data-feed layer rather than the agent logic — if Binance data is intermittently unavailable, the fix requires a data-feed health check upstream of the agent's confidence assignment. A CLAUDE.md rule change alone may not resolve it if the agent is not the source of the bug. Flagging is low-risk; the operational fix requires engineering investigation.

proposed_rule: CONFIDENCE INTEGRITY RULE: The 'confidence' field MUST reflect computed signal quality. Assign confidence as follows: HIGH = signal_score ≥ 3 AND at least 1 oversold signal fired AND R:R ≥ 2.0; MEDIUM = signal_score = 2 OR R:R between 1.5-2.0; LOW = signal_score < 2 OR any required data field is unavailable (RSI=null/?, ADX=null/?). If market data for a symbol is unavailable (RSI=?, ADX=?, regime=?), the cycle MUST log confidence='LOW' and execution_status='SKIPPED' with rejection_reason including 'DATA_UNAVAILABLE: [field]'. Never assign HIGH or MEDIUM confidence to a zero-signal or null-data evaluation cycle. BTC/USDT and other crypto symbols must skip the evaluation cycle entirely (not score and reject) when exchange data fields are null.
